title: Casimir Scaling: Exact in 2D, Approximate in 4D
description: In 2D Yang-Mills (Migdal formula), Casimir scaling holds exactly for all r: the potential ratio equals C₂(R)/C₂(fund). In 4D, exact Casimir scaling fails due to string breaking—after r_break, the adjoint potential saturates while the fundamental grows linearly, so the ratio decreases. The 4D approximate conjecture is axiomatized as open.

meta.author: Migdal (1975); Bali et al. (2000)
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom: casimir_scaling_4d_approximate (the 4D approximate Casimir scaling conjecture). Parts I and II are fully proved: 2D exact scaling follows from Migdal formula; exact 4D scaling fails from string breaking.
originalContributions: twoD_potential_ratio_exact (proved): ratio equals tension ratio for all r > 0
migdalTension_ratio_eq_casimir_ratio (proved): Migdal tension ratio = Casimir ratio
twoD_exact_casimir_scaling (proved): 2D potential ratio = Casimir ratio exactly
exact_casimir_scaling_fails_4d (proved): ratio changes → exact scaling fails

sections.title: Part I Setup: Migdal Tension and Linear Potential
sections.summary: Module header explaining the 2D/4D comparison. Defines linearPotential (area law potential) and migdalTension (σ_R = g²C₂(R)/(2·dim R) from the Migdal formula). Proves migdalTension_pos: σ_R > 0 from g² > 0, C₂(R) > 0, dim ≥ 1.
sections.mathContext: $\sigma_R = g^2 C_2(R) / (2 \dim R)$ (Migdal 1975): the heat kernel on the gauge group gives this exact formula for all representations in 2D. The linear potential $V_R(r) = \sigma_R \cdot r$ holds for ALL $r$ in 2D (no string breaking).

sections.title: Part I: 2D Exact Casimir Scaling Proved
sections.summary: Three theorems prove 2D exact Casimir scaling. (1) twoD_potential_ratio_exact: V_R(r)/V_fund(r) = σ_R/σ_fund for any r > 0 (r cancels). (2) migdalTension_ratio_eq_casimir_ratio: σ_R/σ_fund = C₂(R)/C₂(fund) for same-dimension reps. (3) twoD_exact_casimir_scaling: combines both — the 2D potential ratio equals the Casimir ratio exactly for all r > 0.
sections.mathContext: $V_R(r)/V_{\text{fund}}(r) = (\sigma_R r)/(\sigma_{\text{fund}} r) = \sigma_R/\sigma_{\text{fund}} = C_2(R)/C_2(\text{fund})$. The key: the $r$ factors cancel, giving a distance-independent ratio. In 4D this cancellation breaks when one side saturates.

sections.title: Part II Setup: String Breaking Definitions
sections.summary: Defines saturationPotential (V_R = 2·m_gluelump after breaking) and breakDistance (r_break = 2m/σ_R). Proves breakDistance_pos and the key identity potential_at_break: σ_R · r_break = 2·m_gluelump.
sections.mathContext: $r_{\text{break}} = 2m_{\text{gluelump}}/\sigma_R$: at this distance the energy to stretch the flux tube equals the energy to create two gluelumps. For $r > r_{\text{break}}$: $V_R(r) = 2m$ (constant), $V_{\text{fund}}(r) = \sigma_{\text{fund}} \cdot r$ (still linear, N-ality $\neq 0$).

sections.title: Part II: 4D Exact Casimir Scaling Fails (Proved)
sections.summary: Key inequality: for r > r_break, saturation_lt_linear_post_break proves 2m < σ_R·r (private lemma). post_break_ratio_lt_tension_ratio converts to 2m/(σ_fund·r) < σ_R/σ_fund via div_lt_div_iff + nlinarith. exact_casimir_scaling_fails_4d: the pre-break ratio = σ_R/σ_fund but post-break ratio < σ_R/σ_fund — non-constant, disproving exactness.
sections.mathContext: For $r > r_{\text{break}}$: $\sigma_R r > 2m$ (multiply $r > r_{\text{break}}$ by $\sigma_R > 0$). Then $2m/(\sigma_{\text{fund}} r) < \sigma_R/\sigma_{\text{fund}}$ by cross-multiplication. The ratio is strictly smaller than the Casimir ratio, so it cannot equal it for all $r$ — exact Casimir scaling is disproved.

sections.title: Part III: 4D Approximate Casimir Scaling (Axiomatized)
sections.summary: Defines ApproximateCasimirScaling4D: |σ_R/σ_fund - C₂(R)/C₂(fund)| < ε. Axiom casimir_scaling_4d_approximate: approximate scaling holds at intermediate distances (open conjecture, supported by lattice QCD but not analytically proved). Includes lattice data: SU(2) measured ≈ 2.5 vs Casimir 8/3 ≈ 2.67; SU(3) measured ≈ 2.2 vs Casimir 9/4 = 2.25.
sections.mathContext: $|\sigma_R/\sigma_{\text{fund}} - C_2(R)/C_2(\text{fund})| < \varepsilon$ for $r < r_{\text{break}}$. The deviation $\varepsilon$ arises from non-perturbative effects: string tension receives corrections from gluon self-energy, renormalon divergences, and higher-order operators in the effective string theory.

sections.title: Summary: Complete Answer to OQ-02
sections.summary: casimir_scaling_2d_exact_4d_approximate packages both parts: (1) 2D exact scaling holds for all r > 0 (proved), and (2) 4D post-break ratio < σ_R/σ_fund (proved). Together they answer OQ-02: Casimir scaling holds exactly in 2D, approximately in 4D, and the failure of exactness in 4D is a proved consequence of string breaking.
sections.mathContext: The summary theorem is a conjunction: $\forall r > 0: V_R(r)/V_{\text{fund}}(r) = C_2(R)/C_2(\text{fund})$ (2D, proved) AND $\forall r > r_{\text{break}}: V_R^{\text{sat}}/V_{\text{fund}}(r) < \sigma_R/\sigma_{\text{fund}}$ (4D failure, proved). Together with the axiom, the full picture is formalized.

overview.historicalContext: Casimir scaling in Yang-Mills theory refers to the hypothesis that the string tension ratio $\sigma_R/\sigma_{\text{fund}}$ equals the ratio of quadratic Casimir eigenvalues $C_2(R)/C_2(\text{fund})$. In 2D Yang-Mills, this is an exact consequence of the Migdal formula (1975): the partition function decomposes by representation via the heat kernel on the gauge group, giving $\sigma_R = g^2 C_2(R)/(2 \dim R)$, so the ratio is exactly $C_2(R)/C_2(\text{fund})$ for representations of equal dimension. In 4D, Casimir scaling was observed in lattice simulations by Bali et al. (2000) with high precision for SU(2) and SU(3) at intermediate distances — the adjoint/fundamental ratio was measured within ~7% of the Casimir prediction. However, the theoretical status is subtle: string breaking, the physical mechanism by which a high-energy flux tube snaps to create a particle-antiparticle pair, provides a rigorous reason why exact Casimir scaling cannot hold in 4D for screened (N-ality 0) representations. After string breaking at $r = r_{\text{break}} = 2m_{\text{gluelump}}/\sigma_R$, the adjoint potential saturates rather than growing linearly, causing the ratio to decrease — a proved mathematical fact.
overview.problemStatement: Does Casimir scaling σ_R/σ_fund = C₂(R)/C₂(fund) persist exactly or only approximately in the 4D continuum limit?
overview.text: In 2D Yang-Mills, Casimir scaling holds exactly from the Migdal formula. In 4D, string breaking at r = r_break = 2m_gluelump/σ_R causes the potential to saturate, violating the constant-ratio requirement of exact Casimir scaling. The 4D conjecture that σ_R/σ_fund ≈ C₂(R)/C₂(fund) at intermediate distances is supported by lattice QCD but remains open analytically.
overview.proofStrategy: Part I uses the Migdal formula to show the 2D potential ratio is exactly σ_R/σ_fund = C₂(R)/C₂(fund) for all r > 0. Part II formalizes string breaking: at r > r_break, the adjoint potential is V_R(r) = 2·m_gluelump (constant) while V_fund(r) = σ_fund·r (linear). The key inequality 2·m_gluelump < σ_R·r follows from r > r_break = 2m/σ_R, and div_lt_div_iff converts this to the ratio comparison. The 4D approximate conjecture is axiomatized.
keyInsights: 2D: No string breaking — the area law holds for all representations at all distances, giving exact Casimir scaling
4D: String breaking occurs for screened (N-ality 0) representations like the adjoint at distance r_break = 2m_gluelump/σ_R
After breaking, the potential ratio V_R/V_fund = 2m_gluelump/(σ_fund·r) → 0, contradicting the constant Casimir ratio
The key inequality: r > r_break ⟹ σ_R·r > 2·m_gluelump ⟹ post-break ratio < σ_R/σ_fund
Approximate Casimir scaling (at intermediate r) is observed in lattice QCD but not analytically proved
prerequisites: 2D Yang-Mills: Migdal formula, area law, string tension from heat kernel
String breaking: flux tube energy, gluelump mass, saturation potential
Casimir eigenvalues: C₂(R) for SU(N) representations
Basic real analysis: monotone functions, ratio inequalities

conclusion.summary: Casimir scaling holds EXACTLY in 2D Yang-Mills (proved) and only APPROXIMATELY in 4D (open conjecture). The failure of exactness in 4D is a proved consequence of string breaking for screened representations.
conclusion.implications: The result clarifies why lattice measurements show near-Casimir ratios at intermediate distances: the Migdal formula provides an exact 2D blueprint that gets broken by non-perturbative effects in 4D. Understanding the deviation may illuminate the mechanism of confinement.
openQuestions: What is the precise correction to Casimir scaling in 4D? (perturbative one-loop corrections are known but full non-perturbative treatment is open)
Does Casimir scaling hold in the N → ∞ (planar) limit of SU(N)?
Can the Migdal formula be extended to 3D in a useful approximation?
